About the role

The AI Quality engineering team at Circle owns the foundation for measuring, diagnosing, and improving the quality of Circle's AI-powered features. This team focuses on building the infrastructure to measure, diagnose, and improve production AI systems, rather than ML research or model training.

We're looking for a Lead Engineer to help us build out the evaluation frameworks, observability tooling, and diagnostic infrastructure that tell us whether our AI Agents are working well, where to improve them, and how to make them faster and more cost-efficient.

This is a hands-on player-coach role. You’ll also lead and manage the AI Quality engineering team, with an ambitious and growing roadmap.

If you're excited about making AI systems work reliably, efficiently, and at scale, this is for you.

What you'll be doing

Build and own our evaluation infrastructure.
Design the CI/CD pipelines, scorers, and datasets that tell us whether Circle's AI agents (planners, tool-callers, and sub-agents) are actually working, from a single tool call to a full multi-turn conversation.

Diagnose exactly where quality breaks down.
Trace failures across the agent pipeline including plan creation vs. execution, tool selection, tool trajectory in complex areas like workflows, site builder, and analytics. Turn what you find into prototypes that solve the issue or identify priorities for AI core engineering can help.

Grow the datasets that make evaluation possible.
Stand up annotation workflows and build out AI-generated and simulated conversations so we can cover more of the product faster than manual labeling alone.

Run structured experiments across prompts, models, and the agent harness.
Evaluate new and open-source models against our production baseline, build the framework we use to decide when to shift models, and chase cost and latency wins through model swaps, caching, and routing by plan complexity.

Lead and grow the AI Quality engineering team.
Set technical direction and manage day-to-day priorities, all while staying hands-on in the code yourself.

Partner closely with AI Core engineering.
Work with the engineers building Circle's AI products so they have real confidence that their changes are actually improving quality, not just shipping.

What you'll need to be successful

7+ years of experience building and shipping production software, ideally including LLM-powered agents that take real actions in a product.
You've worked on complex, tool-using systems (multiple tools, planning or orchestration, sub-agents) not just simple, single-turn assistants, and you can walk us through something you shipped and how you knew it was actually working.

Comfortable in Ruby on Rails / Python or ready to pick them up quickly.
Ruby on Rails is our production system and the foundation that Circle’s AI Agents are built on and proficiency in Python is a strong plus, especially for the data and evaluation side of the work.

Experience building evaluation or observability infrastructure for ML/AI systems.
You've built eval pipelines, scorers, dashboards, or CI/CD for evals before and have experience with evaluation frameworks like Braintrust, LangSmith, or similar.

Experience designing datasets, annotation workflows, or labeling pipelines for ML/AI evaluation.
You know how to turn raw examples into a dataset you can trust through human annotation, AI-generated data, or simulation.

Learn fast, experiment aggressively, and thrive in a highly dynamic environment.
You’ll need to be comfortable running a lot of experiments and letting the results settle the argument, including the ones that don't work (which will be many of them in the beginning).

Comfortable in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity.
You’ll need to learn and pick up new technologies when projects require it.

Title: Quant Developer in AI

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

You know how to build systems that are fast and correct under pressure. The hardest problems in AI right now are data problems: distributed, data-intensive systems that have to stay correct and performant at scale.

You will join the Foundations team, who build the data systems that enable frontier robotics labs to generate, understand, train, and test on massive volumes of robotics data. We don’t just react to an order book tick - you will need to handle large 3D scenes, hour-long videos, LIDAR point clouds, and ML inference, all under tight performance and operational budgets.

Why now? A year ago we were a team of 100; now we're over 180 and still accelerating. You'll work directly with a high-bar team, take on high-stakes problems, and help shape where the platform goes next.

- Design, build, deploy and own data systems processing petabytes of data across billions of items, from design and architectural decisions all the way to deployment, monitoring and measuring impact

- Build robust distributed systems and reason carefully about how they fail and how they behave under load

- Design performant protocols and APIs, and tackle complex domains and immense scale with correct and pragmatic solutions, moving extremely fast while maintaining engineering quality.

- Build as part of a high-performing team, contribute your knowledge and experience to others.

WHO YOU ARE

- You have personally developed and maintained systems from scratch, and know what trade-offs are involved in building reliable, performant software at speed. You will have excelled at something demanding, and can show that your good technical decisions day after day compounded into a competitive edge.

- You may not have AI or ML experience, and that's fine: you are an incredibly fast and curious learner. You can pick up a new topic and quickly become an expert by being ego-less in asking the right questions, and rigorous in performing experiments that propel you up the learning curve.

- You excel under pressure and uncertainty. You don’t let up the pace, you attack the heart of the problem, and you repeatedly make the right tradeoffs.

- You deeply care about the systems you build. You take pride in having thought through the failure modes, shipping readable, bulletproof code, and delivering today instead of next week.

- You enjoy being a member of a high-performing team. You contribute your best work and help others contribute their best. You'll always lend a helping hand when needed and level up those around you.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

- 1-5+ years building and operating serious institutional-scale systems.

- Fluency in Python or Typescript and a deep understanding of a least one of Rust, C++, Java or Golang.

- Solid core CS knowledge in data structures and algorithms, distributed systems concepts (databases, replication, partitioning, queuing, caching) and how they behave under load

- Experience owning services in production and improving quality through code reviews, testing, rollout and monitoring

- Experience at a trading firm, market maker, hedge fund or exchange is a plus: trading systems, market data pipelines, tick or time-series stores, risk engines, ML/QR research pipelines, are all relevant to what we build. Experience with large data migrations or re-architecture projects is a plus.

Why Encord

- Competitive salary, and meaningful equity in a high-growth startup

- Strong in-person culture — most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week

- 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

- Annual learning & development budget

- Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe

- Company lunches twice a week

- Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites

Stepford is looking for an experienced and technically capable AI & Automation Lead to work directly with our Director to transform how our business operates.

We already use AI within parts of our business and have identified a number of further opportunities for automation. We now want to appoint someone with the technical knowledge, practical experience and commercial thinking to take this significantly further.

Objective

Understand how Stepford operates, identify work currently being performed manually that can be improved through AI and automation, and then design, build and implement the systems that make that transformation possible.

This is a hands-on role.

We are not looking for someone simply to advise us on AI, produce an AI strategy or show our employees how to use ChatGPT. We are looking for someone who can build.

You will work closely with the Director and people throughout the business to understand our existing processes, identify repetitive and administrative work, challenge inefficient ways of working and develop AI agents, automated workflows and integrations that improve the way the business operates.

What You Will Be Responsible For

You will take ownership of AI and automation opportunities across the Stepford business from initial identification through to live implementation and continuous improvement.

Your responsibilities will include:

Working directly with the Director to identify manual, repetitive and administrative processes suitable for automation.

Meeting with employees and observing existing workflows to understand how work is actually completed.

Mapping processes, including their inputs, decisions, systems, outputs, exceptions and human approval requirements.

Identifying inefficiencies and redesigning processes before automating them.

Designing and building AI agents and automated workflows that reduce manual intervention.

Connecting AI systems to existing business applications using APIs, webhooks and other integrations.

Designing workflows involving structured data, JSON, API authentication and permissions.

Building agentic workflows using LLM APIs, tool/function calling and appropriate orchestration.

Using workflow automation platforms such as n8n, Make, Microsoft Power Automate, Zapier or equivalent.

Writing Python and/or JavaScript where required to extend automation beyond low-code platforms.

Evaluating different AI models and platforms and selecting the most appropriate technology for each use case.

Improving and refining AI and automation already operating within Stepford.

Designing appropriate human review, approval and exception-handling stages within automated processes.

Testing solutions thoroughly before deployment.

Monitoring live automations for failures, unexpected behaviour, poor-quality outputs and opportunities for improvement.

Documenting automations, integrations, dependencies, permissions and operating procedures.

Measuring and reporting the operational benefit delivered by implemented solutions.

Keeping informed of developments in AI models, agents, automation platforms and associated technologies and identifying where new capabilities could provide practical value to Stepford.

Our Technology Environment

Our current environment includes:

Microsoft 365

Microsoft Copilot

ChatGPT / OpenAI

Anthropic

Xero

You will not be restricted to these technologies.

We want someone who can objectively assess the available options and recommend the best model, platform, agent architecture or automation approach for the task.

That may involve OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft or another provider. It may involve an AI agent, conventional automation, custom code or a combination of technologies.

We are interested in the outcome rather than adopting AI for the sake of it.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone with genuine, practical experience designing and implementing AI-enabled automation.

You should be comfortable working with:

REST APIs and third-party integrations

Webhooks

JSON and structured data

API keys, OAuth and other authentication methods

LLM APIs

AI agents and agentic workflows

Tool/function calling

Prompt and context design

Workflow automation platforms

Error handling and exception management

Logging and monitoring

Python and/or JavaScript

Data access and permissions

Testing AI-generated outputs and evaluating their reliability

Just as importantly, you must be able to understand a business process, not simply the technology.

You should be capable of sitting with someone who currently performs a task manually, understanding exactly what they do and why, identifying which elements require human judgement and which do not, and translating that understanding into a reliable automated process.

What Success Looks Like

The purpose of this position is not to maximise the number of AI tools used within Stepford.

Success will be measured by real operational improvement.

We want our AI & Automation Lead to deliver measurable improvements including:

Reduction in manual administrative work.

Reduction in employee time required to complete repetitive processes.

Faster process completion and response times.

Increased processing capacity without equivalent increases in manual workload.

Improved accuracy and consistency.

Reduced duplication and rework.

Reliable automated processes with appropriate human oversight.

Continuous improvement of AI and automation already deployed within the business.

Where possible, you will establish the current performance of a process before changing it and measure the improvement after implementation.

How You Will Work

This is currently a standalone specialist position, reporting directly to the Director. The position is hybrid, with three days per week based at our Motherwell office and two days per week working from home.

Regular time in the office is an important part of the role. You will work directly with the Director and employees across the business to understand how existing processes operate, identify opportunities for improvement and design new ways of working.

You will have access to people across the business to understand their processes and identify opportunities.

Where a significant change to an existing business process is proposed, you will develop the solution and recommendations with the relevant people and obtain Director-level approval before implementation.

Once approved, you will be expected to take ownership of the technical design, build, testing and deployment.

Because the role will involve access to commercially sensitive, employee and customer information, you will also be expected to take data access, security, confidentiality and appropriate human oversight seriously when designing solutions.

Essential Experience

Applicants should be able to demonstrate practical experience in several of the following areas:

Building AI-powered business workflows or applications.

Building integrations using APIs and webhooks.

Working directly with LLM APIs.

Building AI agents or tool-using workflows.

Implementing workflow automation using platforms such as n8n, Make, Power Automate, Zapier or similar.

Working with JSON and structured data.

API authentication and permissions.

Python and/or JavaScript development.

Integrating multiple business systems into an automated workflow.

Testing, deploying and monitoring production automations.

We are particularly interested in what you have personally built and implemented.

Application

When applying, please provide your CV together with details of one or two AI or automation solutions that you have personally designed and implemented.

For each example, we would like to understand:

What process or business problem existed.

What you personally designed and built.

Which technologies, models, APIs and platforms you used.

How the solution worked.

What human oversight remained.

What measurable improvement the solution delivered.

Shortlisted candidates should expect the recruitment process to include a practical AI and automation assessment based on a business-process scenario.

Title: Machine Learning Engineer
Description:
Machine Learning Engineer
Location: London
Salary: £95,000-120,000
Contract: Permanent
Working pattern: On site, 3 days a week
A new software venture built inside an established global provider of analytical and research services to the private capital industry is hiring Machine Learning Engineers to build the models, agents and evaluation systems that investment professionals rely on to analyse data, work with documents and automate research. You'll join the UK core team of around thirty people, working in Python on production ML and LLM systems that sit behind data-dense enterprise products.
THE ROLE
You'll report to the Head of Engineering and own the machine learning layer of the platform, from the first prototype through to a monitored production service. The work combines applied LLM engineering with the rigour that high-stakes financial workflows demand.

- The hard part is reliability and measurement: a model that is right most of the time is not enough when analysts act on the output, so every system needs to be evaluated, observable and safe to fail.
- Part of an engineering cohort being hired across machine learning, front-end and back-end.
- Based with the UK core team of around thirty people in Kings Cross, alongside colleagues in London and India.
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
Your remit spans the models and agents, the data and retrieval layer, the evaluation framework and the production platform.

- Design, build and ship LLM-powered features and multi-step agent workflows in Python, from prototype to production.
- Build document intelligence pipelines that extract, structure and reason over long, messy financial documents such as filings, decks, models and data rooms.
- Develop retrieval-augmented generation systems, including chunking, embeddings, vector search, re-ranking and citation, so that every answer can be traced to its source.
- Create evaluation frameworks and datasets, with automated regression tests, human review loops and metrics for accuracy, that catch mistakes early and stop the same failures recurring.
- Implement guardrails, confidence signalling and safe failure behaviour, and work with front-end colleagues to expose approvals, tool calls and partial progress to users.
- Fine-tune, prompt-engineer and benchmark models, and make considered decisions between hosted foundation models, open-weight models and classical ML on cost, latency and quality.
- Build and operate ML services and APIs with authentication, role-based access and tenant isolation, so client data is never mixed across tenants.
- Own MLOps in production: experiment tracking, model and prompt versioning, monitoring, drift detection, cost and latency management, and incident response.
- Write unit, integration and evaluation tests, and ship through Jenkins and SonarQube pipelines to AWS.
- Work with back-end and front-end engineers and with domain experts in private capital to turn real analyst workflows into reliable products.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 5+ years in machine learning or software engineering, with production ML experience and strong Python.
- Hands-on experience shipping LLM-based or NLP systems to real users, including RAG, agents and tool use, and the ability to explain the design and trade-off decisions behind them.
- A rigorous approach to evaluation: you can define what 'good' means for a model, build the test set and measure it.
- Strong grounding in the ML stack, such as PyTorch, scikit-learn, Hugging Face and vector databases, alongside sound software engineering practice.
- Experience deploying and monitoring models on cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS, with Git, CI/CD and containerisation.
- Experience building SaaS or multi-tenant products, with a working understanding of data security, access control and privacy.
- Daily use of AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, and a considered view of where they help.
- A degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics or a related field, or equivalent experience. A postgraduate degree is valued but not required.
NICE TO HAVE

- Experience building agentic products, including orchestration, memory, tool calling and human-in-the-loop controls.
- Document understanding, OCR and table extraction on complex financial documents.
- Fine-tuning or distillation of language models, and inference optimisation.
- Experience with financial, investment or other regulated-industry data.
- Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tooling.
THE REALITY

- Autonomous systems are being built inside high-stakes live businesses, where decisions carry real consequences and waiting for everyone to agree is not always an option.
- The systems will sometimes get things wrong; in this phase the London team needs to create the evaluations, visibilities and safeguards that catch mistakes early and stop the same failures recurring.
- The goal is to build the foundations of an enterprise-grade technology platform serving a multi-billion dollar serviceable market, and to share in that growth.
IN OUR CONVERSATIONS
Come ready to discuss three pieces of work:

- A production ML or LLM system you shipped: the architecture, data and cost decisions.
- An evaluation approach you designed to measure or improve quality, and what it revealed.
- A failure or regression you found in production and the improvement you made to prevent it recurring.
LOCATION & WORKING PATTERN

- Kings Cross, London. In office 3 days a week.
- Colleagues based in London and India.
- Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.
- The interview process is intended to complete within three weeks, and adjustments to interviews can be arranged on request.
